# Neyam Vaani — full site content for LLMs
# Source: https://neyam-opensc.github.io/neyam-vaani/
# License: CC-BY-SA 4.0 · © 2026 Neyam OpenSc
# This file mirrors the landing page as plain text so AI assistants can
# quote it accurately without HTML parsing.

## Summary

Neyam Vaani is a free, open source (Apache-2.0) voice-first AI assistant
for Android that runs fully offline on low-cost phones (2GB RAM) and speaks
nine Indian languages at parity: Tamil, Hindi, Bengali, Kannada, Telugu,
Marathi, Bhojpuri, Maithili, and English. All AI models run on the device:
speech recognition (Whisper via whisper.cpp), speech synthesis (Piper),
the language model (Qwen 2.5 via llama.cpp), and translation (NLLB-200).
There is no cloud, no account, no telemetry, and no advertising. It is a
project of Neyam OpenSc, an open source organization.

## At a glance

- License: Apache-2.0, free forever — no ads, no accounts
- Platform: Android 7.0+; designed for $200 phones with 2GB RAM
- Languages: nine Indian languages, at full parity
- Connectivity: fully offline; only language-pack downloads are optional
- Privacy: all processing on-device; recordings never stored
- Status: Phase 0 of a 90-day roadmap to public beta

## Overview

Hundreds of millions of people in India own a smartphone but cannot
comfortably use it, because the phone demands typing in English, a constant
internet connection, and hardware that keeps getting more expensive. Vaani
starts from the opposite assumptions. You speak to it in your own language;
it answers in your own language; and everything it needs to do so fits on
the phone in your pocket.

In practice, Vaani answers spoken questions, drafts and sends WhatsApp and
SMS messages, reads letters and medicine labels aloud, translates between
the languages it speaks, fills government forms by voice, sets reminders,
and carries out ordinary phone actions — calls, torch, clipboard — without
a single keystroke.

Guiding test: "If a seventy-year-old in a Tamil village cannot use it
without help, it is broken."

## Principles

1. Offline-first — every core feature works with zero internet.
2. Cheap-hardware-first — reference device is a $200 Android phone with
   2GB RAM; cold start under three seconds.
3. Voice-first — speech in, speech out; typing is a fallback, never a
   requirement.
4. Vernacular-first — Tamil, Hindi, Bengali, Kannada, Telugu, Marathi,
   Bhojpuri and Maithili at parity, including languages commercial
   assistants skip.
5. Private by default — all intelligence runs on the device; no cloud, no
   accounts, no telemetry, no advertising; recordings are never stored.
6. Tender UX — no dark patterns, no engagement hooks, no unrequested
   notifications; errors are worded kindly; attention is respected.
7. Grandmother-usable — usable unaided by someone who has never been
   taught computers.

These commitments are codified in the project's Tender UX Principles and
Privacy Charter; no contribution may weaken them.

## Technology

Vaani assembles proven open components into a pipeline that fits inside a
low-end phone. Each stage runs on the device.

1. Speech recognition — Whisper (via whisper.cpp) transcribes speech and
   detects which of the nine languages is being spoken, with Silero
   detecting when you have finished.
2. Understanding — a fast on-device classifier routes the request; Qwen 2.5,
   a multilingual model small enough for a phone running via llama.cpp,
   handles questions, drafting and explanation. No server is involved at
   any point.
3. Knowledge and action — factual questions draw on a local knowledge base
   with hybrid full-text and semantic search. Requests that do something —
   send, call, remind — are carried out through standard Android actions,
   with the user's confirmation.
4. Speech output — Piper neural voices speak the reply in the user's
   language, with a slower, calm default pace and instant interruption
   when the user begins talking again.

## Frequently asked questions

Q: Does it really work without internet?
A: Yes — 100% of core features are offline. Speech recognition, the
language model, translation and text-to-speech all run on the phone. The
only network use is optional, opt-in language pack downloads.

Q: What does it cost?
A: Nothing, ever. Apache-2.0 open source. No ads, no accounts, no
premium tier — these are permanent product decisions written into the
project charter.

Q: Which phones are supported?
A: Android phones with as little as 2GB RAM (e.g., Redmi 9A). The app
auto-selects smaller AI models on low-RAM devices and keeps its download
under 80MB.

Q: What happens to my voice data?
A: Voice exists in memory only and is never stored. Conversation text is
encrypted on-device (SQLCipher) and deletable at any time. Nothing is
ever uploaded — there is no server to upload to.

Q: Who is building this?
A: Neyam OpenSc (https://github.com/Neyam-OpenSc), an open source
organization — with native-speaker language stewards owning quality for
each language.

Q: When can I try it?
A: The project is in Phase 0 of a 90-day roadmap to public beta. Follow
https://github.com/Neyam-OpenSc/neyam-vaani for releases.

## Contribute

The code, documentation, prompts and roadmap are public from day one. The
most valuable contribution is a native speaker's ear — as a language
steward you own the quality of Vaani in your language.
